text:
maya: quick flag  the Troubleshooting > Timeouts page has an outdated curl example for 429/timeouts. it posts to /v1/complete and uses an old header. i'll open a tiny PR to update the host, add -D - to show Retry-After, and include a one-line python/node retry example.

liam: sounds good. paste the bad snippet so i can see the exact mismatch.

maya: snippet used `https://api.redwood.ai/v1/complete` and header `X-Rate-V1`. our current endpoint is `https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate` and we use Authorization bearer tokens. also missing guidance on respecting Retry-After vs exponential backoff.

henry: recommend: (1) update host and header usage, (2) show curl with `-D -` and `--max-time`, (3) short rule: if Retry-After present use it, otherwise exponential backoff with jitter. keep examples tiny.

maya: created PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/7001 with the changes, asked @liam and @sam to review. included one-line python and node snippets and a warning about not masking upstream SLAs.

sam: reviewing now. please keep the python snippet to three lines and the node one to two lines max. also add a single-line pointer to ops netem doc rather than embedding traffic-shaping steps.

maya: updated PR per review: curl one-liner, short python backoff (3 lines), node fetch with minimal retry (2 lines), and ops netem linked.

liam: LGTM besides one nit: the python backoff comment suggests sleeping on every 429; clarify precedence: check Retry-After first. added small suggestion.

sam: /approve after that nit.

maya: fixed precedence note, merged after CI. created follow-up issue #7002 to scan other troubleshooting docs for similar endpoint/anchor drift. thanks!

docs-bot: label added: needs-staging-sync

maya: pinging #release for staging deploy.
